summary: Full end-to-end verification of AI Video Clipping Laboratory (backend + frontend). 14/14 backend tests passed (real Whisper transcription + real Claude claude-sonnet-4-6 analysis, no mocks). Full UI flow verified: upload -> live status polling -> READY in ~15s -> transcript with speaker pills + clickable timestamps -> 3 clip candidates with expanded scores panel (8 sub-metrics + overall) -> preview seeks player -> single Generate produces real mp4 with Download -> Generate All finishes remaining clips -> delete clip + delete job work. Whisper produced 13 segments matching the known espeak script (words 'invest', 'mistake', 'market', 'money', 'time' all present). Claude produced real titles/hooks/reasons with EDUCATIONAL content-type detected and per-clip scores like Hook=92, Standalone=98, Social Appeal=91. Range streaming returned 206 with correct Content-Range/Accept-Ranges. Corrupt-mp4 upload correctly returned 400 (not 500). Non-video extension correctly rejected 400. Bad provider name correctly rejected 400. AI feature verdicts: whisper-transcription - PASS (13 real segments, keyword overlap 5/5); claude-analysis - PASS (3 clips with real, non-boilerplate reasons and per-metric scores); clip-render (FFmpeg) - PASS (real mp4 with ftyp box downloaded). Skills loaded: ai-testing-core, ai-testing-audio, ai-testing-llm.
critical_code_review_comments: Studio.jsx line 95: TranscriptViewer's onSeek uses `ref.current?.seek(t)` but `ref` here is the forwardRef received by CenterStage - it's the same object as centerRef in the parent, so this works, but it's a slightly confusing pattern. Consider using an internal ref instead.

server.py generate_all schedules a background task then returns immediately - the returned {'generating': N} number is only the initial pending count. UI polls state so it recovers, but the response is a bit misleading (does not confirm which clips will actually be re-processed). Not a bug.
Streaming route _range_response returns 200 (FileResponse) when a client sends a non-Range GET; that's correct HTTP behavior. If clients rely on always seeing 206 they'd be wrong.
pipeline.py catches broad `Exception` and marks job as error - good. But the error message includes `str(e)` which could leak internal paths in production. Fine for personal-use local app.
seed_data_creation: Tests upload and clean up their own job using /app/backend/storage/test_video.mp4 (already present in repo).
context_for_next_testing_agent: The single class TestPipelineLifecycle in test_pipeline.py must stay a single class (loadscope pins to one xdist worker so test_a...test_j run sequentially and share `_shared` dict). The test video at /app/backend/storage/test_video.mp4 is a 42s solid-color frame with real espeak speech from /app/backend/storage/script.txt (about investing). Real Whisper+Claude are exercised via EMERGENT_LLM_KEY in /app/backend/.env. Full pipeline ~15s.
ai_feature_verdicts: whisper-transcription (primary): pass - evidence: 13 real segments, transcript contains 5/5 expected keywords from the espeak script (invest, mistake, market, money, time); tested via `POST /api/videos/upload` + poll `/api/videos/{id}`.

claude-analysis (primary): pass - evidence: 3 clip candidates returned with real distinct titles/hooks/reasons (e.g. 'The Biggest Investing Mistake Nobody Talks About') and per-clip 8-metric scores (Hook=92 Standalone=98 Payoff=98 Info=88 Emotional=70 Curiosity=85 Context=95 Social=91); detected_content_type=educational (not the user-picked 'auto').
ffmpeg-clip-render: pass - evidence: single clip generation returned status=generated, downloaded file's first 32 bytes contain the 'ftyp' MP4 box; Generate All completed 3/3 clips.
